It does so the way Unidata’s series does — the learner records a response per exercise in a separate handbook, scores it against the rubric, and the trainer scores the same entries — with one addition the series does not have: a roll-up per objective, so that the handbook gives one verdict per objective. ), so the row now covers seven of the eight steps of the step → failure table — framing (1, 2), data (3, 4), split (5), train (3), validate (7), refine (8, 9) and test (10); justify is counted under O2 (Entries 9 and 11). The entries that must be Proficient are the two the step table names as the leakage and test lessons (5 and 10) and the one that carries O2’s “justify honestly” (11); the counts leave room for one weak data entry and one weak refinement entry without failing the objective. This table is the home of each entry’s objectives: the tags on the handbook’s entry headers and in the criteria table’s second column are derived from it and must match it row for row — O1 and O2 only, the two objectives this notebook serves.

No promotion means the register’s first incumbent — the rung-0 Niño-sign rule — was the model tested in 3g; the sign rule was made incumbent as the physical prior, not because it cleared the always-wet bar, so Entry 10’s interval lines are where its skill is read. The same holds after a promotion: the 3f rule promotes over the incumbent, not over the base rate, so a promoted model’s skill is still read from the interval lines, and a learner who reads “promoted” as “skilful” caps at
